tuning.note: Dawn draw (sim/happenings.ts): from minDay, once minGapDays have passed since the last happening began, chancePerDawn to start one (at most maxActive at a time). (event, town) pairs are weighted by event.weight x town weight: 1, plus biasWeight for a townBias town, plus whenWeight where the event's `when` holds, plus playerTownWeight where the player woke. townBias names roles (den/home: your home hearth, or a generated district's den-like town; village, town, city; despairing; lit) or authored town ids (the den maps to the den role, a missing town to the nearest gap). `when` reads the town (sim/happening-world: starving, foodCoverBelow, despairAbove, legitimacyBelow, litAtLeast, hasCreed, newChapelWithin, deathWithin, atWar, warNearby, collapsedWithin, any); an event whose `when` fails there does not happen there, and one cause (a death, a war, a fallen doctrine) is told once per town. townStrict events only happen in their bias towns. say/news/newsHere may be lists of variants ({town}, {name}: the speaker, {target}: who it fell on, {dead}). relapse.mul effects make burning people in that town lose relapseFlamePerDawn x (mul - 1) flame each dawn they last.

events.name: Grey Rain
events.blurb: The sky rinses color out of the streets. Even revived hands slow.
say: Grey rain. Even the mended ones are slowing.
This rain gets in under the skin. Look how slow they move.
Grey all the way down today. Keep your coal dry.
news: Grey rain over {town}. {name} says even the mended ones are slowing.
It rained grey on {town} all morning. {name} says nobody lifted their head.
{name} says {town} woke to grey rain, and the lit ones felt it first.

events.name: Stranger with Embers
events.blurb: A traveler cups a dying coal and asks if you still know how.
say: A stranger came through cupping a coal. Asked after someone who still knows how.
There was a traveler at the well with a coal in both hands. Asking for you, I think.
Someone came through with embers. Wouldn't give a name, only asked who still tends fires.
news: A stranger with embers passed through {town}. {name} says they were asking after someone who still knows how.
{name} says a traveler came to {town} carrying a dying coal, asking who still knows the way of it.
A stranger in {town} cupped an ember at every door. {name} says they moved on before noon.
newsHere: A stranger cups a dying coal by the {town} hearth and asks if you still know how. You do. {name} watches it catch.
A traveler holds out a coal gone nearly black. You breathe on it and it answers. {name} sees.
At the edge of {town} a stranger offers you their last ember. It takes to your hands. {name} stops to look.

events.name: Bad News Rider
events.blurb: Hoofbeats. A letter. Someone's almost-healed crack splits.
say: A rider came at first light. {target} read the letter twice.
The rider didn't even get down. {target} hasn't spoken since.
Hoofbeats before dawn, and a letter for {target}. Bad, by the look of it.
news: A rider brought bad news to {town}. {name} says {target} took it hard.
{name} says a rider came to {town} with a letter, and {target} went grey reading it.
Bad news rode into {town} at first light. {name} says it was for {target}.

events.name: Market Ghost
events.blurb: Stalls stand like ribs. Trade feels like a rumor.
say: Stalls standing like ribs. Nobody's buying.
Market day, and not a soul at the stalls.
I set out my table and packed it up again. Nobody came.
news: The market in {town} stood empty this morning. {name} says trade feels like a rumor.
{name} says the stalls in {town} stood bare all morning.
No market to speak of in {town} today. {name} says even the sellers stayed home.

events.name: A Child Laughs
events.blurb: Short. Bright. Unreasonable. It helps more than it should.
say: Did you hear that? A child, laughing.
Somebody's little one is laughing at the geese. Listen.
That laugh. When did we last hear one of those?
news: A child laughed in {town}, short and bright. {name} says it helped {target} more than it should.
{name} says a child's laugh carried across {town}, and {target} smiled for the first time in days.
In {town} a child laughed at nothing. {name} says {target} hasn't stopped humming since.
newsHere: Somewhere in {town} a child laughs. Short. Bright. {name} looks up, and so does {target}.
A child's laugh rings across {town}. {target} turns toward it like a plant to light. {name} grins.
A laugh, small and sudden, somewhere in {town}. {name} catches your eye. {target} is smiling.

events.name: Rumor of the Hill
events.blurb: Children say the hill walks. A shutter unlatches from the wrong side — a breach for something large.
say: The little ones say the hill walks. I don't laugh at it.
A shutter came open from the outside last night. Something big, the children say.
They say the hill came down to drink. I found the mud on the step.
news: Children in {town} say the hill walks. {name} found a shutter unlatched from the wrong side.
{name} says the children of {town} swear the hill moved in the night.
A rumor in {town}: the hill walks. {name} says a door stood open that nobody opened.

events.name: Den Goes Cold
events.blurb: You pushed through the night without banking the den fire. Morning takes its cut.
say: Nobody banked the den fire. It's cold in here.
The den's gone cold. Ash and nothing.
Somebody should have seen to the den fire.
news: The den fire went out while you were away. {name} says the hollow in {town} is cold this morning.
{name} says the den in {town} went dark in the night. Nobody banked it.
Word from {town}: the den fire died while you were gone. {name} says the stones are cold.

events.name: Bread Riot
events.blurb: Empty bellies find the granary door. Promises get thrown back at whoever made them.
say: They broke the granary door. There was nothing behind it.
Bread, they shouted. Then they shouted the names of the ones who promised it.
I saw {target} throw the first stone. Hunger did the rest.
news: There was a bread riot in {town}. {name} says the granary was empty when they got in.
{name} says {town} went hungry once too often. The crowd turned on the ones who promised bread.
Hungry folk filled the square in {town}. {name} says the old promises were shouted back, word for word.
newsHere: The square in {town} fills with hungry people. {name} is among them, shouting for bread nobody has.
A crowd breaks the granary door in {town}. It is empty. {name} stands in the ruin of it, shaking.
In {town} the hungry turn on the ones who promised. {target} throws the first stone; {name} does not stop them.

events.name: Festival
events.blurb: Lanterns strung between the roofs. Somebody found a fiddle.
say: Lanterns tonight! Someone's found a fiddle.
Half the town's lit. Seems a shame not to dance about it.
They're stringing lights between the roofs. Come and see.
news: {town} is holding a festival. {name} says there are lanterns strung across every street.
{name} says {town} danced half the night, and nobody can remember why it started.
Word from {town}: a festival, music and lanterns. {name} says even {target} came out for it.
newsHere: {town} strings lanterns between the roofs. {name} pulls you into the dance, and something in you catches.
There is music in {town} tonight. {target} is laughing; {name} presses a warm cup into your hands.
A festival in {town}: fiddles, lanterns, bread from somewhere. {name} says you should stay for the last song.

events.name: Funeral
events.blurb: A stone is set. Those who were closest stand nearest the hole.
say: We put {dead} in the ground this morning.
{target} hasn't left {dead}'s stone since the burying.
They sang for {dead}. Badly, but they sang.
news: {town} buried {dead}. {name} says {target} stood at the stone long after the rest went home.
{name} says the whole of {town} turned out to lay {dead} to rest. {target} took it worst.
A funeral in {town} for {dead}. {name} says {target} could not sing for crying.
newsHere: {town} gathers at the new stone for {dead}. {target} stands nearest; {name} keeps a hand on their shoulder.
They lay {dead} to rest in {town}. {name} says a few words. {target} says none.
A slow line walks {dead} to the stones outside {town}. {target}'s flame gutters. {name} stays close.

events.name: Refugees
events.blurb: Carts piled with bedding. Faces that will not say what they saw.
say: Carts on the road all morning, piled with bedding. Running from the fighting.
Families from the war, sleeping in the barn. Somebody gave them the last of the bread.
They won't say what they saw over there. You can see it on them anyway.
news: Refugees from the fighting have reached {town}. {name} says there's no room, and they're making room.
{name} says {town} is full of folk fled from the war, sleeping wherever there's a roof.
Carts of people running from the war came into {town}. {name} took a family in.
newsHere: Carts roll into {town} piled with bedding and children. Running from the war. {name} is already counting blankets.
Strangers from the fighting fill the square in {town}. {name} hands out bread and watches the road behind them.

events.name: Power Vacuum
events.blurb: The old creed fell. Nobody holds the keys yet, and everyone is trying the doors.
say: Nobody's in charge since it fell. Everyone's trying the doors.
The old promises are gone and nothing's taken their place. Folk are listening to anyone.
Three people stood on the steps today claiming to speak for the town.
news: Since the doctrine fell, {town} has no one holding the keys. {name} says anyone with a voice is being heard.
{name} says {town} argued in the square all day over who speaks for it now.
{town} is between masters. {name} says it's frightening, and a little bit like air.
newsHere: In {town} the old creed's banners come down and nothing goes up. {name} says folk will listen to anyone now. Even you.
{town} has no one in charge. {name} stands on the steps and asks who will say what comes next.
